land.text: 'By 1870 the empire covered much of what is now the southeastern Democratic Republic of Congo'; the Upemba Depression and the left bank of the Lualaba

successors.note: 'In 1889 it was split in two by a succession dispute, ending the unified state, and later joined the Congo Free State.' Msiri's Yeke kingdom had already taken the south-east (Yeke page: it 'stopped the southwards expansion of the Luba Empire').

capitals.name: Mwibele
capitals.note: APPROXIMATE: the Luba Empire infobox gives 'Capital: Mwibele (today in Haut-Lomami)' with no year and no coordinates; the point is the middle of the gazetteer's Lake Upemba, standing in for the Upemba Depression. The Luba people page names the royal sacred village Kitenta, where Ilunga Sungu was venerated.

correction.text: the Upemba Depression ('Luba settlements were built around lakes and marshes'), the Luba core on the upper Lualaba

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Luba): 'founded by King Kongolo around 1585' in the Upemba culture area; the pages give no boundary or area, so the first empire is a 120 km disc on Lake Upemba (confidence 1 for the shape). The Luba people page says only that the Luba 'began to coalesce into a single, unified state' 'around 1500, possibly earlier'.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'The Luba Empire greatly expanded its influence during the period from 1700-1860' and 'By 1870 the empire covered much of what is now the southeastern Democratic Republic of Congo' (Luba people page). No area is given; the gazetteer's 'Luba (region)' (230,000 km2, bbox 22.5-28.5 E, 10-5 S, confidence 1) stands in and is held to 1889. It overlaps Katanga, where Msiri's Yeke kingdom held the south-east from the 1860s, so the south of this shape is overdrawn after 1867.

region.text: the Upemba Depression ('Luba settlements were built around lakes and marshes'), the Luba core on the upper Lualaba

ledger.note: c. 1585: the Luba Empire is founded in the Upemba Depression. 'The Luba Empire was founded by King Kongolo around 1585'; the Luba people page: the Luba 'began to coalesce into a single, unified state' 'around 1500, possibly earlier', and the Luba Empire page leaves 'Established' blank and notes that dates run from the 8th to the 15th century (Congolese historians) to the 18th (some Western scholars). 1585 is the date nearest to a founding in the pages.

region.text: 'By 1870 the empire covered much of what is now the southeastern Democratic Republic of Congo'; the Upemba Depression and the left bank of the Lualaba

ledger.note: 1700-1860: the Luba empire expands. 'The Luba Empire greatly expanded its influence during the period from 1700-1860'; in the 19th century 'the Luba began invading their neighbors to set up their own vassal tributaries' (three 'fire kingdoms', the first of them founded before 1810). The page names no land; the region is the gazetteer's Luba region.

ledger.note: 1889: the Luba Empire ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1889'; 'In 1889 it was split in two by a succession dispute, ending the unified state, and later joined the Congo Free State.' [Reviewer af-06, 2026-10-19: confidence lowered from 3 to 2: the Luba Empire page says 'In 1889 it was split in two by a succession dispute, ending the unified state, and later joined the Congo Free State', so the year is the page's but the hand-over to the Free State is 'later', not 1889, and the region is the gazetteer's 'Luba (region)', which the page does not name]

wars.name: Luba-Kanyok conflict and Ilunga Sungu's expansion
wars.outcome: Ilunga Sungu 'expanded into new territories and formed marriage alliances after a conflict with the Kanyok around the start of the 19th century'; he died in 1810.
wars.note: No land is named; the years are approximate.

wars.name: Msiri and Arab-Swahili incursions into Luba lands
wars.outcome: 'By the 1850s, slavers began intruding into the Luba people lands'; Msiri 'raided and took over the southeastern Shaba region'; breaches from several sides 'weakened the Luba Empire rapidly between 1860 and 1880s'.
wars.note: The pages date none of the Luba losses to a year, so the ledger records no loss event.

certainty.note: A kingdom of tributary chiefs; no frontier is given by the pages.

notes: Cliopatria has no Luba. The pages give no boundary or area, so the shapes are a disc on Lake Upemba and the gazetteer's 'Luba (region)' (confidence 1). The founding year is 1585 from the Early Congolese history page; the Luba people page says 'around 1500, possibly earlier' and the Luba Empire page leaves it blank. Not settled: the land and year of Msiri's seizure of the south-east, Kikondja and the Kazembe/Lunda splits, the Luba-Lunda marriage that founded Lunda (Lunda page), the ruler list. Capital coordinates are a stand-in. Page budget (2-5): three pages.
